work.permit: Permit from the Minister responsible for labour (Child Care and Protection Act, section 35)

note: Work: the Child Care and Protection Act, 2004 (as printed with L.N. 111/2005), section 33: no one may employ a child under thirteen in any work; section 34(1): a child of 13 to 15 only in an occupation on the prescribed list of light work; so the form holds 15 for general employment (my reading of sections 33 and 34; the Ministry of Labour and Social Security's page says the same: under 13 illegal, light work 13 to 15). Section 34(3) bars hazardous and night work for any child (under 18). Section 35: notwithstanding sections 33 and 34, the Minister responsible for labour may, on the Council's advice, issue a permit for a child to be employed in artistic performances, setting hours and conditions; no lower age is set. The Child Care and Protection (Amendment) Bill, 2023 (on Parliament's site) wasn't read for these sections. Read from the Georgetown Global Food Laws collection's scan of the Act (the Ministry of Justice's laws site didn't answer). Majority: the National Land Agency says that by the Law Reform (Age of Majority) Act a person attains majority and is of full age at eighteen, and a minor's contracts are voidable; the Act itself (Ministry of Justice laws site) didn't answer. Service: no conscription law was found; left null.

sources.title: Georgetown Global Food Laws: Jamaica, Child Care and Protection Act 2004 (scan of the printed Act)
sources.said: No person shall employ a child under the age of thirteen ... No person shall employ a child who has attained the ... age of thirteen years, but who has not attained the age of fifteen ... the Minister responsible for labour may, on the advice of the ... issue a permit to a child to enable that child to be ... employed for the purpose of participating in artistic performances.

sources.title: Ministry of Labour and Social Security (Jamaica): Child Labour
sources.said: This Legislation makes it illegal to employ children who are less than 13 years old, however it permits light work between the ages 13 to 15 years.

sources.title: National Land Agency (Jamaica): Dealings with a minor
sources.said: By virtue of the Law Reform (Age of Majority) Act a persons shall attain the age of majority and be of full age on attaining the age of eighteen (18) years.
